issues.legal_issue: The central revisional authority may revise a custodian’s order in an evacuee-property proceeding continued under successor legislation.
material_facts: The proceedings concerned whether the respondents were evacuees and whether their properties were evacuee property.
The proceedings began under an earlier state law, but successive saving provisions treated actions and proceedings under that law as taken or commenced under the successor laws.
The Custodian-General reviewed the Custodian’s order under the central law and, after hearing the parties, set it aside and directed fresh disposal.
issues.conclusion: The Custodian-General had jurisdiction to revise the Custodian’s order, and the revisional order was not liable to be quashed as jurisdictionally invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 conferred broad power to call for the record of proceedings in which a Custodian had passed an order and to examine its legality or propriety. The successive saving provisions in s. 53(2) of the Mysore Administration of Evacuee Property (Second) (Emergency) Act, 1949 and s. 58(2) and (3) of the 1950 Act, as amended with retrospective effect, carried earlier proceedings into the successor regime. In light of the central Act’s purpose of establishing a central administration of evacuee property, the origin of a proceeding under the earlier state law did not exclude revision.

predicates.evacuee_property_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the administration or status of property claimed to be evacuee property.
predicates.proceeding_carried_into_successor_regime: A proceeding begun under an earlier law was treated by successor legislation as continuing under the successor regime.
predicates.custodian_passed_order_subject_to_centra: A Custodian passed an order in the proceeding, and the central regime placed such orders within the central revisional authority’s review.

issues.definition: When an evacuee-property proceeding is carried into a successor regime and a Custodian has made an order subject to central review, the central revisional authority may validly review it.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal from a Custodian’s order in a proceeding continued under successor legislation lies under the successor appeal scheme rather than under a repealed law’s appeal provision.
material_facts: The claims began under an earlier state law that allowed appeals to the High Court.
The earlier state law was repealed, and saving provisions treated proceedings begun under it as proceedings under successor legislation.
The successor legislation provided an appeal to the Custodian-General from the relevant kind of Custodian’s order.
The High Court treated the earlier appeal provision as continuing to govern and heard the appeals.
issues.conclusion: No appeal lay to the High Court from the Custodian’s order; the successor legislation’s appeal forum superseded the earlier High Court appeal forum by necessary intendment.
issues.legal_principle: A right of appeal is a substantive right that ordinarily accrues when proceedings commence and is not taken away absent express provision or necessary intendment. Under s. 53(2) of the second Mysore Act and s. 58(3) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, proceedings begun under the first Mysore Act were treated as proceedings under the successor laws. Because the investigation under the earlier procedure was in substance equivalent to the investigation under the successor procedure, and the successor laws provided a different appeal forum, the successor appeal scheme displaced the earlier one by necessary intendment. The Court relied on Garikapatti Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhury, [1957] S.C.R. 488.

predicates.appeal_from_custodian_order: The proceeding seeks to appeal a Custodian’s order concerning evacuee property.
predicates.proceeding_started_under_repealed_evacue: The proceeding began under an earlier law that was later repealed.
predicates.proceeding_carried_into_successor_regime: Successor legislation treated the earlier proceeding as one under the successor regime.
predicates.successor_regime_provides_different_appe: The successor legislation provides an appeal forum different from the one provided by the repealed law.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a Custodian’s order in a proceeding begun under a repealed law, carried into a successor regime that provides a different appeal forum, the earlier appeal forum is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Certiorari does not permit an appellate re-examination of factual findings where the decision-maker had jurisdiction and no reviewable legal error is shown.
material_facts: The writ petitions challenged the Custodian’s decision that the respondents were evacuees and their properties were evacuee property.
Whether the respondents were evacuees was a question of fact.
The Custodian had jurisdiction to decide the matter after the Custodian-General’s valid revisional order.
The High Court re-examined the Custodian’s decision as an appellate court, and no jurisdictional error or patent error of law justifying certiorari was established.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in interfering under Article 226 by reviewing the factual finding or treating the writ proceedings as an appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226, certiorari is supervisory, not appellate. It may correct jurisdictional errors, specified illegality in the exercise of jurisdiction, or a patent error of law apparent on the face of the record, but it does not permit review of factual findings merely because they may be erroneous. The Court applied the principles in Hari Vishnu Kamath v. Syed Ahmad Ishaque, [1955] 1 S.C.R. 1104.

predicates.constitutional_certiorari_proceeding: The proceeding seeks supervisory review of a decision by a lower authority through a constitutional writ of certiorari.
predicates.challenged_decision_made_with_jurisdicti: The authority that made the challenged decision had jurisdiction to decide the matter.
predicates.dispute_turns_on_facts: The issue decided by the authority principally concerns factual findings.
predicates.no_patent_error_of_law_or_other_reviewab: The record discloses no patent legal error or other error that warrants supervisory correction.

issues.definition: In a certiorari proceeding, where the challenged decision was made with jurisdiction, the dispute turns on facts, and no reviewable error is shown, supervisory interference is unavailable.
